meta.brief: US-first pricing, NGO/conservation weighted, mostly under $50, all links HTTP-checked 2026-08-20

items.item: Lemon shark organic cotton onesie (Lucky Bug Clothing Co.)
items.desc: Made in New York from organic cotton, and the lemon shark print is a direct Sharks4Kids collaboration — rare to find species accuracy on a babygro.
items.ngo: 10% of all lemon shark print sales go to Sharks4Kids (shark conservation and education)

items.item: Great white shark organic cotton baby bodysuit (PADI Gear)
items.desc: "Sharks are jawesome" print on 100% organic cotton; the obvious gift for diver parents.
items.ngo: Not stated on the product page (PADI's charity is the PADI AWARE Foundation, but no donation is claimed for this item)

items.item: Infant shark onesie (Shedd Aquarium shop)
items.desc: Combed organic cotton from an accredited public aquarium's own store; stock rotates, so the search link is the durable one.
items.ngo: Shedd Aquarium (non-profit — store proceeds support the aquarium)

items.item: Kids' organic cotton shark tees and long sleeves (Shark Trust)
items.desc: Organic cotton, printed to order in a renewable-energy UK factory, so nothing is made until it's bought — and the species artwork is actually correct.

items.item: Sharks4Kids apparel range (Redbubble)
items.desc: Tees, hoodies and leggings in designs made with Sharktopia; the same artwork also comes as cheap stickers if you want a stocking filler.
items.ngo: Sharks4Kids (proceeds fund their education and outreach programmes)

items.item: "Sharks are older than trees" youth tee (Fin Pin Shop)
items.desc: The single best shark fact, worn as a shirt. Run by marine biologists, so the merch reads like it was written by someone in the field.
items.ngo: Fin Pin Shop states purchases support wildlife conservation and scientific research (percentage not published)

items.item: MISS logo tees, hoodies and sticker packs (Minorities in Shark Sciences)
items.desc: Wearing this says something. The annual Shark Madness sticker collections are the pick if you want something small and collectable.

items.item: OCEARCH tees and caps
items.desc: Instantly recognisable to anyone who has ever followed a tagged white shark on the tracker; the Jawbone and Don't Fear designs are the strongest.
items.ngo: OCEARCH (funds shark research, tracking and free education programmes)

items.item: Save the Sharks bamboo socks (Bare Kind)
items.desc: Bamboo, comfortable, and the packaging carries the conservation story — a good low-stakes gift for someone who already owns enough shirts.
items.ngo: 10% of profits to a shark conservation charity (Bare Kind partner: Love The Oceans). UK seller, ships internationally

items.item: Socks that Protect Sharks (Conscious Step)
items.desc: Fairtrade, GOTS and vegan certified, with the donation baked into the price rather than bolted on.

items.item: Socks that Protect Whale Sharks (Conscious Step)
items.desc: Same deal, spotted variant. Buy both and you've solved two colleagues at once.

items.item: Great white shark necklace (Cape Clasp)
items.desc: Sterling silver charm on a 20" adjustable chain, made in collaboration with the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy — subtle enough for the office.
items.ngo: 15% of profits to the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy

items.item: Hammerhead, whale shark and thresher jewellery range (Cape Clasp)
items.desc: The widest species range in shark jewellery: hammerhead, great white, whale shark, thresher, manta, and a mermaid's purse cuff for the egg-case nerds.

items.item: Bimini Shark Lab apparel
items.desc: Hats, tees, tanks and hoodies from the field station a lot of us trained at. Note: the classic logo apparel is Bimini-only — the online shop carries the rest.
items.ngo: 100% of funds raised go to the Bimini Biological Field Station Foundation

items.item: Shark Trust adult clothing (organic, print-on-demand)
items.desc: Tees, sweatshirts, hoodies and totes in organic cotton, made to order in a renewable-energy factory. Returnable to be remade when worn out.

items.item: Sharks4Kids official merch (Bonfire)
items.desc: Campaign-based drops rather than a permanent range, so worth checking what's live before December.

items.item: Atlantic White Shark Conservancy limited-edition merch (Bonfire)
items.desc: Limited runs funding white shark research, public safety and education on Cape Cod.

items.item: Whale shark crop hoodie and enamel pins (Fin Pin Shop)
items.desc: Marine-biologist-run; the pins and stickers are the cheapest way to give someone something that is unmistakably theirs.
items.ngo: States that purchases support wildlife conservation and scientific research (percentage not published)

items.item: White shark ecokin plush, 12" (Monterey Bay Aquarium)
items.desc: Fabric and fill are 100% recycled PET — sixteen water bottles per shark — and the proportions are actually right.

items.item: Mako shark plush, 15" (Monterey Bay Aquarium)
items.desc: Also 100% recycled bottles. A mako rather than yet another great white, which is half the appeal.

items.item: Whale shark plush, 20" (Wild Republic)
items.desc: Big, soft, and spotted in roughly the right pattern; meets CPSIA and EN71 safety standards so it's safe for the very small.

items.item: Cuddlekins mako shark, 15" (Wild Republic)
items.desc: The washing-machine-survivor tier of plush. Also available as great white and blacktip.

items.item: OCEARCH plushie
items.desc: A cuddly white shark whose purchase funds the tracking of real ones.

items.item: Sharks TOOB — 11 mini figurines (Safari Ltd.)
items.desc: Eleven hand-painted species in one tube — great white, whale, tiger, hammerhead, mako and an eagle ray — for the price of one plush. Best value on this list.

items.item: LEGO Creator 3-in-1 shark sets
items.desc: The current Fierce Shark with a Treasure Chest (31381, 379 pieces, 8+) rebuilds into an anglerfish or a manta ray. Category link given because set numbers retire.

items.item: Shark tooth fossil dig kit (National Geographic)
items.desc: Chisel a brick apart to excavate replica teeth, then string one as a necklace. Chisel, brush and magnifier included; ages 6+.

items.item: Mini fossil dig set with real shark teeth, 2-pack (Discovery #MINDBLOWN)
items.desc: Genuine fossil teeth rather than replicas, and every one is different — which is the bit children actually care about.

items.item: Mission Ocean cooperative board game (Adventerra Games)
items.desc: Cooperative rather than competitive, playable from about four, and built from recycled materials. Ocean plastic is the theme.
items.ngo: Part of proceeds to The Ocean Cleanup

items.item: Sharkopoly board game
items.desc: Twenty-two species, each with its own profile card of facts. It is exactly what the name suggests, which is the point.
items.ngo: Not stated — seller is a commercial shark-content site, not a registered charity

items.item: 4D Vision great white shark anatomy model
items.desc: 13" model, 20 detachable organs and a display stand, with an anatomy guide. The closest thing to a dissection that lives on a shelf.

items.item: Oceans (North Star Games)
items.desc: A serious strategy game about evolving marine species, designed with a marine biologist and painted in watercolour by Catherine Hamilton. Top 1% on BoardGameGeek. Ages 12+, 60–90 minutes.

items.item: "Ray of Hope" 1000-piece jigsaw (Shark Trust)
items.desc: Caribbean reef sharks, 1000 pieces, and the money goes somewhere useful.

items.item: OCEARCH 1000-piece puzzle
items.desc: Same idea, different charity, and it pairs well with the tracker app on a rainy afternoon.

items.item: Sharks 1000-piece jigsaw (Eurographics)
items.desc: Over 25 species laid out as an identification plate — you finish the puzzle and you've learnt the sharks.

items.item: Shark Block — Christopher Franceschelli
items.desc: Chunky die-cut board book with fold-out flaps introducing real species. Survives being chewed, which is the operative test.

items.item: Good Night Sharks
items.desc: Bedtime book covering white, whale, bull and angel sharks — an unusually broad species list for ages 2–5.

items.item: Shark Lady: How Eugenie Clark Became the Ocean's Most Fearless Scientist — Jess Keating
items.desc: The picture-book biography of Eugenie Clark. Named a Best STEM Book by the Children's Book Council and the NSTA, and the one book on this list most likely to produce another shark scientist.

items.item: Sharkpedia (2nd edition) — DK
items.desc: Scrapbook-style reference on anatomy, species, myth and media, with a conservation and take-action section added in the second edition. Grades 2–6.

items.item: Sharks4Kids colouring and activity books
items.desc: Written by shark educators, including a Sharks of Florida colouring and activity book. Buying direct sends the money to the programme.

items.item: Sharks Don't Sink: Adventures of a Rogue Shark Scientist — Jasmin Graham
items.desc: Memoir by a MISS co-founder on being a Black woman in shark science. The book to give a teenager who is being quietly discouraged from the field.
items.ngo: Not applicable (trade publisher) — author co-founded Minorities in Shark Sciences

items.item: A Pocket Guide to Sharks of the World — Ebert, Fowler & Dando
items.desc: Every shark family in a book that fits in a jacket pocket, with Marc Dando's illustrations. A real ID guide at a teenager's price point.

items.item: Shark Girl — Kelly Bingham
items.desc: YA novel in verse about a fifteen-year-old rebuilding her life after a shark bite. Fiction, and a useful counterweight to the monster framing.

items.item: Why Sharks Matter — David Shiffman
items.desc: The book to hand anyone who asks what you actually do all day, and the one that argues the conservation case without the doom.

items.item: Chasing Shadows: My Life Tracking the Great White Shark — Greg Skomal & Ret Talbot
items.desc: Skomal on the white shark's return to the eastern seaboard, and on doing science while the public panics.

items.item: Sharks of the World: A Complete Guide — Ebert, Dando & Fowler
items.desc: 536 species, fully revised. The reference copy for a lab shelf rather than a coffee table.

items.item: Field Guide to Sharks, Rays & Chimaeras of Europe and the Mediterranean
items.desc: Regional guide for European colleagues and anyone working the Med.

items.item: Field Guide to Sharks, Rays and Chimaeras of the East Coast of North America
items.desc: The east-coast companion volume. Between the two, most of the northern hemisphere is covered.

items.item: Sharkpedia: A Brief Compendium of Shark Lore — Daniel Abel & Marc Dando
items.desc: Small, illustrated, and browsable — the shark book for someone who already owns the serious ones. Not to be confused with the DK children's title of the same name.

sections.title: 🤿 Equipment & ocean gear
sections.note: Sub-headed by kind rather than age — note a size/age in the entry where it matters.

items.item: Aqua Lung Sport Kid's Mix Combo mask and snorkel set
items.desc: Top children's pick in DiveIn's tested round-up. Linked to the review rather than a retailer because stock and pricing move; buy from whichever dive shop has the size.

items.item: Reef Tourer youth single-window mask & snorkel set
items.desc: The budget option that still seals properly on a small face — which is the whole game with children's masks.

items.item: Kids' UPF 50+ zip rash guards (SwimZip)
items.desc: Blocks 98% of UVA and UVB, and the full-length zip is what makes it possible to get a wriggling toddler into it.

items.item: Shark-print UPF 50 sun shirts (Berry Jane)
items.desc: Shark prints in Oeko-Tex inks, chlorine resistant. Site search for "shark" — individual prints rotate each season.

items.item: RSPB Handbook of the Seashore
items.desc: The book that turns a bucket of unidentified beasts into a species list. UK/European shores.
items.ngo: Not applicable — RSPB-branded (RSPB is a conservation charity)

items.item: Waterproof sharks and rays ID cards (Franko Maps)
items.desc: Laminated, hole-punched for a lanyard, and available as region-specific sharks-and-rays cards for the Caribbean, Bahamas and elsewhere. Cheap and genuinely used in the water.

items.item: 4D Vision great white shark anatomy model
items.desc: Also listed under Toys & games — it works as a teaching aid as much as a toy. 20 detachable organs, ages 8+.

items.item: Shark tooth fossil dig kits
items.desc: Excavation brick, chisel, brush and magnifier. The Discovery version contains real fossil teeth if you'd rather they dug up the genuine article.

items.item: Shark colouring book with stickers
items.desc: Die-cut into the shape of a shark's head, FSC-certified paper, and a sheet of sea stickers in the back.

items.item: Sharks of Florida colouring and activity book (Sharks4Kids)
items.desc: Regionally specific, which is unusual and much more useful than generic shark art.

items.item: Whales & sharks washi tape (Cognitive Surplus)
items.desc: A science-stationery brand's take on cetaceans and sharks; the cheapest thing on this list that still feels considered.

items.item: Oceanic 31 art prints (Shark Trust)
items.desc: Species prints — silky, Galapagos, basking, smooth hammerhead, and a larger Carcharodon carcharias — from the Oceanic 31 campaign. Frame-worthy office art.

items.item: Shark stickers and enamel pins (Fin Pin Shop)
items.desc: "Sharks are older than trees", "sharks are older than Saturn's rings" — field-nerd humour done properly. Laptop and field-notebook decoration.
items.ngo: States that purchases support wildlife conservation and scientific research (percentage not published)

sections.title: 🌊 NGO & branded merch
sections.note: One sub-section per organisation. List your full range here, and feel free to also tag individual items up in sections 1–5 with your org's name so age-browsers don't miss them.

items.item: Full range: adoptions, clothing, prints, jigsaw, books
items.desc: Digital shark adoptions £25 worldwide, printed packs £25 UK-only; clothing on a separate print-on-demand site; Oceanic 31 prints £35–75. The most complete single-org range on this list.

items.item: Full range: apparel, headwear, plush, puzzle, stickers
items.desc: Tees $29.99–39.99, hoodies $49.99–69.99, plushie $29.99, 1000-piece puzzle $24.99, can cooler $12, sticker pack $20.
items.ngo: OCEARCH — funds shark research, tracking and free education programmes

items.item: Full range: books, apparel, lemon shark adoption
items.desc: Colouring and activity books, Redbubble and Bonfire apparel, an Adopt a Lemon Shark programme, and partner discount codes (Stream2Sea reef-safe sunscreen, Alohi Kai jewellery).

items.item: Full range: stickers, tees, hoodies, posters
items.desc: Includes the annual Shark Madness sticker collections. Main site: misselasmo.org.
items.ngo: MISS — supports gender minorities of colour entering marine and shark science

items.item: Shark Shop apparel
items.desc: Hats, tees, tanks, crops, hoodies and long sleeves. Classic logo apparel is sold in Bimini only; occasional Bonfire fundraising drops online.
items.ngo: 100% of funds to the Bimini Biological Field Station Foundation

items.item: Merch, jewellery and a Massachusetts licence plate
items.desc: Bonfire limited editions, the Cape Clasp great white necklace, and a Paul McPhee-designed MA plate ($40, of which $28 is tax deductible). Physical shops in Chatham and Provincetown.
items.ngo: AWSC — all shop proceeds fund research, education, public safety and conservation

items.item: Recycled-plastic plush, toys, apparel, books
items.desc: The ecokin plush line is made from 100% recycled PET. Broad enough to cover several age bands from one shop.

items.item: Marine-species jewellery
items.desc: Not an NGO itself, but 15% of profits go to marine non-profits, with specific pieces tied to named partners (the great white necklace supports AWSC).

items.item: Shark shop
items.desc: US organisation working since 2006 to reduce the shark fin trade; merch supports that campaigning.

items.item: Shark adoptions and apparel — shop currently being rebuilt
items.desc: Virtual and plush shark adoptions plus apparel. Flagged because shop.sharkangels.org now redirects to an update notice, so check availability before recommending it as a gift.

items.item: Ocean-inspired apparel and accessories
items.desc: Graphic tees and accessories. Note that "Save Our Seas" is also a generic slogan on Redbubble, Etsy and elsewhere — this is the Foundation's own shop.

sections.title: 🎁 Wildcard / miscellaneous
sections.note: Anything that doesn't fit above — experiences, subscriptions, digital, advent calendars, etc.

items.item: Adopt a Shark — digital pack (Shark Trust)
items.desc: Great white, whale, hammerhead, basking or oceanic whitetip. Personalised certificate, factsheets, poster and bookmark; the money funds research and campaigns rather than one animal. Digital version ships worldwide.

items.item: Adopt a Shark — printed pack (Shark Trust, UK only)
items.desc: The physical version, for recipients who want something to open. UK delivery only.

items.item: Adopt an Animal (Mote Marine Laboratory & Aquarium)
items.desc: Three adoption tiers starting with a $30 e-adoption (personalised certificate and fact card). Sharks among the species available.

items.item: Adopt a Lemon Shark (Sharks4Kids)
items.desc: Supports conservation research, and it's a lemon shark rather than the usual great white.

items.item: Shark Tracker+ subscription (OCEARCH)
items.desc: Follow real tagged sharks, with shop discounts included. A gift that keeps arriving as pings all year.

items.item: Shark encounter or dive immersion (Aquarium of the Pacific, Long Beach CA)
items.desc: Up-close animal encounter on select days, or a full dive for certified divers daily.

items.item: Out to Sea Shark Dive (Wonders of Wildlife, Springfield MO)
items.desc: SeaTREK helmet dive with sand tiger and sandbar sharks, no diving certification needed.

items.item: Eye-to-Eye shark dive gift ticket (Point Defiance Zoo & Aquarium, Tacoma WA)
items.desc: Sold specifically as an undated gift ticket for up to four divers, which solves the "they can't commit to a date" problem.

items.item: Aquarium membership (Georgia Aquarium and others)
items.desc: A year of visits rather than one afternoon. Most accredited aquariums run an equivalent — pick whichever is nearest the recipient.

items.item: Whale shark conservation volunteering (Maldives, Mafia Island, Belize)
items.price: Hundreds to low thousands — serious splurge
items.desc: For the person who wants to give something enormous. Research placements rather than tourist swims, which is the ethical distinction that matters here.
items.ngo: Varies by placement — check the individual project

items.item: "Shark Attack Pack" fossil advent calendar (Code Black Fossils)
items.desc: Seven days, a genuine fossilised shark tooth behind each door. The only advent calendar here that leaves you with something real.

items.item: 24-day 3D-printed sea animals advent calendar
items.desc: Twenty-four articulated ocean animals including sharks; doubles as a fidget-toy stash after December.
